clue.text: Had ambitions, when pride was hurt

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

indicators.note: something hurt is damaged, so the word pride gets its letters knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone once aimed high until their pride took a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' looks like part of the story of wounded pride, but 'was hurt' is the anagram signal; 'when' gives the opening piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim for something lofty, so someone who aspired was harbouring hopes.

clue.text: I master troubled goddess

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters of I master are jumbled

explanation.surface: A teacher confesses to being bothered by a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the seven letters of I MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek deity of the hunt and the moon, an example of a goddess.

clue.text: Do what you like may I insist, in person

parts.note: a polite pressing request, 'Please!', is a way of saying may I insist
doing something yourself means doing it in person

explanation.surface: A request to act freely, politely pressed and delivered face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom granting permission: act as you wish.

clue.text: Free hand to travel

parts.note: to rid something of a burden is to free it
E, East, is one of the four hands at a bridge table

explanation.surface: With a hand freed up, someone sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players, or hands, are named North, South, East and West, so 'hand' can give E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to go on a journey by horse, bike or vehicle, a kind of travelling.

clue.text: Men go wrong in unlit country

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for unlit

parts.note: something unlit is dark

indicators.note: going wrong means going astray, so the letters of Men are put out of order

explanation.surface: Men lose their way in the gloom of some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wrong' scrambles the three letters of the men, and 'in' places them within the word for unlit.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Fellow in the bay

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a chap or man
a small sheltered inlet on a coast

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an old slang word for a chap, and a small sheltered inlet of the sea.

clue.text: Study seal, say, from hide

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: say signals that the word seal is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: the sea animal, given as written before being voiced

explanation.surface: Someone watches a seal, perhaps from a birdwatcher's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a hide as a shelter for watching wildlife; it is the verb meaning keep out of sight. 'say' marks SEAL as heard, spelt CEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight, a synonym of the verb hide.

clue.text: Huge tub full of sulphur

indicators.note: full of means the word for tub holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a vat is a large tub or tank
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: An enormous tub brimming with sulphur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts S inside VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vast is immense, so it is a synonym of enormous.

clue.text: Wrongly gather harem is to be scattered

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about, so harem is gets rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone misunderstands that a sultan's harem is to be dispersed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be scattered' rearranges HAREM IS. 'gather' here means understand, not collect.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather can mean to understand from what is heard, so catching words incorrectly is getting it wrong.

clue.text: Goodness! Luck with roll-up for head judge

parts.note: Lord! is an exclamation of surprise like Goodness!
chance means luck or fortune

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word roll is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a roll is a register or list, given as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone's good fortune with a hand-rolled cigarette, said about a top judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A roll-up is a hand-rolled cigarette, which hides the split: 'up' reverses the word for a list. The Lord Chancellor is a senior British office.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chancellor was historically the head of the judiciary in England and Wales, the senior judge.

clue.text: Annoy by encroaching, as person on foot does?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to offend someone by intruding on their area
a walker literally steps on their own toes, read in jest

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the idiom for giving offence by intruding, and a literal picture of a walker stepping on toes.

clue.text: Assemble for service

definitions.meaning: A church service in the Catholic tradition

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for crowding together, and the Eucharistic church rite.

clue.text: Drink is magnificent to knock back

indicators.note: knock back means the word for magnificent is turned round

parts.note: regal means splendid, fit for a king

explanation.surface: A drink so magnificent it must be downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like drinking but reverses REGAL. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a pale beer, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Lied about having nothing to do

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of Lied are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told fibs about being unoccupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle is unoccupied, without work or tasks.

clue.text: Poet died at stake

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family records
the ante is what is at stake in a poker game

explanation.surface: A poet perished at the stake like a martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests burning at the stake; the ante is a poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy, an example of a poet.

clue.text: One is introduced to fat landowner

indicators.note: being introduced to the word for fat means being put inside it

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is introduced to a portly estate owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is introduced to' puts I inside LARD. A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the proprietor of an estate, so a property holder of land.

clue.text: Fool about with high flyer

definitions.meaning: to play pranks and mess around
a songbird that sings while soaring high

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for messing about playfully, and a songbird known for soaring.

clue.text: Allow woman to hold a polisher

indicators.note: to hold means the words for allow and woman together surround the next letter

parts.note: to let is to allow
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Let a woman take hold of the shoe polisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' places the letter A within the two joined pieces. A wash leather is the British name for a chamois cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamois or wash leather is a soft skin used for buffing cars and windows to a shine.

clue.text: Make opposing move from desk

definitions.meaning: the serving desk in a shop or bank

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for hitting back or opposing, and a shop's serving surface.

clue.text: Was irritable, dropping apple on to earth

indicators.note: in a down clue placing one thing on to another puts the first above the second

parts.note: a crab is a crab apple, a small sour wild apple
a bed is a patch of earth in a garden where plants grow

explanation.surface: Someone grew cross when an apple fell on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' is a link that completes the picture: CRAB dropped on to BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To crab is to grumble or complain, so having crabbed means having been grumpy.

clue.text: Criticise wine, having understanding

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise sharply
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Critics savage a wine while sharing a sympathetic bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close sympathetic relationship, a mutual feeling of harmony.

clue.text: Difficult position traps old public officer

indicators.note: the word for a difficult position traps, or encloses, the next letter

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in a tight spot

explanation.surface: A tricky situation catches out an elderly official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' puts O inside CORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is an official who investigates sudden deaths, a public office holder.

clue.text: Church more suited for cathedral staff

parts.note: apter means more apt, more suitable

explanation.surface: A church is a better fit for the clergy of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: A chapter is the body of canons who run a cathedral, a sense many solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The canons who govern a cathedral are collectively its governing body of clergy.

clue.text: Always turned down accepting fib for comfort

indicators.note: accepting means taking the next word inside
in a down clue turned down means the word for always is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ever means always
a lie is a fib

explanation.surface: Someone who always refuses to believe a fib finds it a consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned down' reverses the word for always, giving REVE in this down clue, and 'accepting' takes the fib inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to ease their distress, a synonym of the verb soothe.

clue.text: Some cheap seats in far end of church

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the budget seating is found at the back of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'in', a link word; an apse is the far end, not 'in' it, so the definition is 'far end of church'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, behind the altar.

clue.text: Slender bough seen in fine mist

definitions.meaning: a small branch with leaves or flowers

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a small flowering twig, and a cloud of tiny droplets.

clue.text: Huntsman's strip?

definitions.meaning: John ... was the Cumbrian huntsman of the song 'D'ye ken John ...'
to strip off a skin or layer

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is: the huntsman is a strip. John Peel was an English fox-hunter celebrated in a folk song.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a famous fox-hunter from an English folk song, and a verb for removing an outer layer.

clue.text: Bushy hairstyle, for a change

indicators.note: a change rearranges the letters of for a

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a big hairdo for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges FOR A; 'for a change' reads as one idiom in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, full style of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: Be amused-half smile

indicators.note: half says to take only the first half of the letters of Be amused

parts.note: the run sits at the start of these words because the setter halves them, not by a coincidence of hiding: the first half is the pick

explanation.surface: Being amused raises a half smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first four of the eight letters in BE AMUSED. The surface reads 'half smile' together; the dash splits them.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to grin broadly, a synonym of the verb grin.

clue.text: Sudden dash by university athlete, a complete surprise

definitions.meaning: read literally, a bolt is a sudden dash and a Blue is an Oxbridge athlete, so a sprint coming from such a runner
the idiom describes an unexpected event, like lightning from a clear sky

explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a literal sprint from a university sportsperson, and the idiom for an unexpected shock.

clue.text: Refuses to destroy town!

indicators.note: destroying the word town breaks it up so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone declines to raze a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroy' rearranges TOWN; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying will not is a contraction expressing refusal.

clue.text: Pity about TV detective

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of the British TV series

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry about a television sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse was a long-running British TV detective drama set in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity and remorse both describe a feeling of sorrowful regret.
